title: Default-on commit attribution: Claude co-author trailer + session URL now appended to commits and PRs (rolled out via auto-update)
description: A recent Claude Code release (2.1.24x/25x series, late Aug 2026) turned commit attribution on by default: via auto-update the CLI began appending a 'Co-authored by: Claude' trailer and a claude.ai session URL to commit messages and PR descriptions, with no release notes or opt-in prompt. A maintainer indicated it applies to web and Remote Control sessions. The change ignited HN's biggest Claude Code thread of the week (177 points, 201 comments on 2026-08-30).

community_feedback.quote: I cancelled my subscription over this
I really hate this attribution nonsense ... it fires even if you audit every line and add your own changes too, which means the attribution is misleading
This is probably a controversial take, but I love this. [session-ID tagging] is a lifesaver when debugging old commits
It's not meant for saying 'this change was done by Claude' it's meant to connect commits back to the session
[Defaulting it on without release notes is] clownshoes ... though having the feature available seems good
Claude started inserting session links in PRs and commits without asking — it's spamming both, and the links can expose your full prompt history
There's a third option under attribution to set false — attribution/sessionUrl — to prevent Claude from adding session links
Do you let Claude co-author your commits/PRs? Some developers actually find co-author tags useful for tracking which agent wrote what
Developer elaborated in a tweet that he cancelled his Claude subscription over the silent default-on attribution change
GitHub issue #90142 (Aug 27): make the '🤖 Addressed by Claude Code' reply signature optional — users keep asking that Claude's attributions be opt-in, not always applied

title: OpenAI terminates Cursor partnership following Cursor's acquisition by SpaceX; current models available only until ~Nov 12
description: OpenAI published a post explaining it is ending its partnership with Cursor after Cursor's acquisition by SpaceX, citing trust concerns ('we cannot be confident that SpaceX will use our technology within our terms of service') and Musk's past testimony on xAI model distillation. Existing OpenAI models remain available to Cursor users until the contract end date (~Nov 12, 2026); OpenAI's upcoming 'Astra' model will not be offered. Cursor's CEO says OpenAI models are only ~5% of usage and is emailing customers about 'continuity of access to OpenAI models'. Discussed heavily on HN (832 points, 524 comments, 2026-08-29).

community_feedback.quote: According to Cursor CEO, it only accounts for 5% usage of cursor, so it's not a big deal at all
It's basically not going to affect them at all. I don't know a single person that uses OpenAI models via Cursor.
I have never seen one large company throw another large company under the bus without any legalese filters
If you have such a world changing technology, why sell an API when you can capture all the value yourself?
A pretty standard circling of the wagons in preparation for the next phase in the battle for frontier AI dominance
Top comment speculates OpenAI fears SpaceX would train models on all the LLM responses Cursor users receive — the same way Elon has done previously
Cursor will have no users left before its own acquisition by SpaceX is completed
Last night, OpenAI said it was ending its partnership with Cursor because SpaceX acquired it. The Altman-Musk rivalry gets its latest chapter
SpaceX bought Cursor for its user base, that's it. There is nothing revolutionary (in 2026) about Cursor's coding harness

title: Rapid release week: 0.151.0 (MCP tool-result interception, plugin catalogs), 0.150.0 (@ task mentions, Interrupt hooks), 0.149.0 (agents dashboard, queue)
description: Codex CLI shipped four stable releases in the window: 0.151.0 (2026-08-29) adds a configurable MCP tool-discovery grace period, lets extensions inspect/replace MCP tool results before they reach the model, and combines per-repo plugin catalogs with hardening fixes (sandbox enforcement, subagent token budgeting); 0.150.0 (2026-08-26) introduces @-mentions to reference other Codex tasks, a /copy picker, auto-generated task titles, and Interrupt hooks; 0.149.0 (2026-08-20) adds a `codex agents` dashboard, `codex queue`, and expanded diagnostics. Platform-wide, scheduled tasks can now trigger from Gmail/Slack/GitHub events (2026-08-25) and `codex mcp-server` was deprecated in favor of the Codex app server (2026-08-24).

community_feedback.quote: Codex CLI 0.150.0/0.150.1 is a meaningful task-to-task workflow, TUI, hooks, security, MCP, and Bedrock release
codex remote-control fails with 'connection is errored' on 0.150.1 (Linux Mint 22.3)

title: v2.1.251 release — PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch hooks, subagent live streaming to Remote Control, security and reliability fixes
description: Claude Code 2.1.251 adds PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch hook events (block/confirm/annotate model switches), live streaming of foreground subagent tool calls to Remote Control clients, a spend-limit bar in /usage, and per-session prompt-cache stats in /cost. It also fixes a symlink-following file-tool security issue and dozens of reliability bugs. Released ~2 days ago alongside a rapid-fire series (2.1.246–2.1.250) over the past week.

community_feedback.quote: Issue tracker is very active against the 2.1.24x/25x series: WezTerm shifted-punctuation regression reported on 2.1.247 (#90067) and glibc 2.44 segfaults on native builds (#89564/#89420)

title: Weekly releases Aug 24: Customize tab GA, Copilot CLI native Rust runtime, VS Code 1.135 agents layout, Visual Studio August update, JetBrains harness GA
description: GitHub Copilot's Aug 24 weekly drop (published 2026-08-28) makes the Copilot app Customize tab GA (MCP servers, plugins, skills, canvases in one place), adds a native Rust runtime to Copilot CLI with defaultMode/defaultPermissionMode settings and mid-turn session recovery, and ships VS Code 1.135 with cross-app agent session resume, 'second opinion' model checks, and a new single-pane Agents layout. Visual Studio gains pinned favorite models, org-wide shared custom agents, and plan consumption views; the Copilot harness in JetBrains is now GA with built-in MCP server support (public preview) and /review integrations.

title: Origin code hosting beta, cloud agent Builds, Subscriptions, custom modes, and /goal
description: Cursor launched Origin, its own code hosting in early beta for paid plans (repos, PRs, two-way GitHub sync, Vercel/Depot/Buildkite apps), and shipped cloud-agent improvements: Builds (3x faster starts), event Subscriptions for PRs/Slack/scheduled tasks, skills as pinned Custom Modes, isolated subagents on their own VMs, /goal for long-lived objectives, and non-interrupting steering. Published 2026-08-27.

title: Aug 26 release: minute-level automation scheduling, code scan v3 API with batch remediation, one-click OAuth MCP installs, new session UI with nested Sub-Devin tree
description: Devin shipped two major updates in the window: on 2026-08-26, automations gained minute-level scheduling, multi-channel triggers, and an 'Improve with Devin' action; code scans moved to /security with a 'Scan now' button, batch remediation via new v3 API routes, and streamlined in-card OAuth for MCP marketplace installs; queued messages now deliver during long-running waits. On 2026-08-21, the session experience was redesigned (customizable sidebar tabs/grouping/filters, nested Sub-Devin session tree, session subscribers), Devin Review got scan profile editing and effort selection (normal/deep), and enterprise-level MCP server configuration plus private-network MCP support landed.

community_feedback.quote: r/CognitionLabs update roundup (through Aug 27): Devin Fusion is now 4% more intelligent and 27% less expensive on FrontierCode 1.1
'Where did Devin go?' threads on r/ChatGPTCoding/r/webdev debate Cognition's ~$25-26B valuation and whether Devin is living up to it

title: v0.57.0 stable — capacity-aware silent retries, multi-turn rollback on cancel, IDE directory fix; security nightlies (MCP OAuth SSRF fix, fail-closed workspace trust)
description: Gemini CLI's latest stable v0.57.0 (2026-08-25) adds context-aware silent retries with availability TTL for capacity errors, rolls back the entire multi-turn request on cancellation/abort, dynamically resolves Cloud Workstations proxy redirect URIs for OAuth, and fixes a swallowed directory mismatch in IDE connections plus several SSR Agent issues. The v0.58.0-preview.0 line isolates Docker/container-runtime sockets in macOS Seatbelt and declares top-level safety checkers in write policy; nightlies through Aug 29 add an MCP OAuth metadata-discovery SSRF fix and fail-closed workspace trust with mcpServers filtering in restricted mode.

title: New GitHub Copilot experience in Slack (public preview) + shared agentic work in Microsoft Teams
description: Copilot's agentic CLI/app capabilities arrive in Slack as a public preview: mention @GitHub in a DM, channel, or thread to start an agent session that can triage bugs, investigate failures, implement changes in a secure cloud sandbox, and open PRs. GitHub is a launch partner for Slack Code ('a new type of channel designed for agents'), sessions are shared/multiplayer by default and can continue from PR to terminal, Copilot app, or IDE. Copilot Business/Enterprise only; usage counts against cloud agent budgets. A parallel update brings shared agentic work to Microsoft Teams. Announced 2026-08-21.

community_feedback.quote: Any way to trigger a Copilot background agent from Slack? — a long-standing r/github request this feature finally answers; users suggest assigning issues to Copilot as a workaround
Users on r/GithubCopilot wish for Slack/text notifications when agents need input during sessions

title: v3.8.20 — Agent Command Center multi-window, Devin Local plan mode with reviewable Markdown plans, cloud live shell streaming (Windsurf IDE now 'Devin Desktop')
description: The former Windsurf IDE (rebranded 'Devin Desktop' under Cognition since v3.0.12, June 2026) shipped v3.8.20 on 2026-08-21: Agent Command Center now follows the selected space, converts an editor window in place, and supports unlimited side-by-side agent windows; Devin Local gains multi-root/virtual workspaces, a plan mode that writes a reviewable Markdown plan with an explicit 'Implement' button, and mid-turn subagent stopping; Devin Cloud adds live shell output streaming and session URL sharing. Released 2026-08-21.
